prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests compared to noise-corrected results.
Evidence is still thin for all tested change types (adoption/redesign, choose_path/reorder, home/wait_info, sign_in/notification) as each has only a single test so far.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: -6.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, reorder: +1.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: +4.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, notification: +1.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 86.8%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 19.0%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Controls Interactive Guide: Insert a dedicated interactive desktop controls guide screen right after the welcome screen to teach users how to move, talk to, and hide their pet. (why: 3 support emails reported user confusion on how to control, hide, or talk to their pet after onboarding, while the finish step has a 64.8% completion rate.)
1: [finish, new_flow] Pet Render Verification Flow: Add an interactive display verification step in home_intro to confirm the pet successfully rendered on the desktop and troubleshoot missing pet issues. (why: 3 support emails reported that the pet does not show up on desktop or the app will not open after completing setup.)
2: [sign_in, hint] Multi-Account Restore Sign-In Hint: Display a hint on the sign-in screen explaining that logging into an existing account recovers previously created pets. (why: 8 support emails (the top support theme) reported pets missing or reset after signing in with different accounts.)
3: [home, notification] Desktop Notification Toggle During Wait: Provide a desktop notification toggle on the waiting screen to alert users when pet generation is finished. (why: The waiting step takes over 38 minutes on average (mean 2336s), causing users to leave the app unattended.)
4: [choose_path, copy] Engaging Story Value Proposition Copy: Rewrite story screen headline and body copy to clearly explain desktop pet interactivity and set instant expectations. (why: Early drop-off at choose_path (76.2% conversion) happens within a median of 8s due to lack of immediate product context.)
5: [finish, layout] Stage Layout Welcome Banner: Update home_intro screen to a prominent stage layout featuring step counters and a clear completion action button. (why: Finish step conversion drops to 64.8% with an extremely long mean duration (5815s), showing users stalling at the final step.)

scores.note: Requires a new screen; only 3 support emails and past redesign/screen addition tests showed negative lift (-6.2%).
High development cost for a new verification flow with limited evidence and low historical confidence for new flows.
Strong evidence as the top support theme (8 emails) with a low-cost copy/hint tweak on a high drop-off step (27.1%).
Directly addresses severe duration friction (38m mean wait time) matching previous home/wait_info success (+4.0%).
Config-only copy tweak addressing fast 8s drop-off at choose_path; aligns with modest positive prior test (+1.8%).
Targets high finish step drop-off (35.2%), but layout redesigns have low confidence due to prior negative test (-6.2%).
